workstream: C: agent SDK (@bondline/sdk) and MCP server (@bondline/mcp) - independent verification

verified.evidence: npm run typecheck -w @bondline/sdk and -w @bondline/mcp both exited with no errors.

verified.claim: SDK end-to-end on a fresh Anvil passes (10/10)
verified.evidence: Ran a copy of sdk/test/e2e.test.ts patched only for port/chain id 8562 and foundry out dir out-vc (copies in verification/vc, symlinks to the real src). 10 pass, 0 fail. The shipped test hardcodes 8551, so I did not run it as shipped.

verified.claim: MCP over stdio with a real MCP client passes (8/8)
verified.evidence: Same patched copy of mcp/test/mcp.test.ts on port 8562: 8 pass, 0 fail.

npm run test:live -w @bondline/sdk: 4 pass. I also read bond() and reserved() on all four testnet offer covers with cast and they equal what the CLI printed: live#0 25300000/5940000, live#1 26250000/6000000, replay#0 44166666/20000000, replay#1 25500000/9900000.

verified.claim: Quickstart works literally from a clean shell
verified.evidence: env -i PATH HOME zsh -f: npm install ok (package-lock.json md5 22c92352f36bcf9a622826507957fe5e before and after), npx bondline offers --listed returned 4 offers, quote returned ok true premium 1000000 principal 99000000 reservationNeeded 19800000 free 19360000, record careful returned hasRecord false generatedAt 2026-10-03T21:58:32.645Z, node mcp/bin/bondline-mcp.mjs answered an initialize request on stdio with serverInfo bondline 0.1.0. The docs snippet (Bondline + configFromEnv, listOffers, quoteCover, getAgentRecord) also ran: 2 listed live offers, quote ok, premium 1000000, record name Careful.

verified.claim: One signature, one transaction underwriting; typed data is correct
verified.evidence: On my chain via the MCP client: the typed data domain hashed (viem hashDomain) to the USDG on-chain DOMAIN_SEPARATOR read by eth_call (0x05d7882d...a9d, equal true). Message from=underwriter, to=market, value=500000000, validAfter 0, validBefore = now+3600. After the create tx the underwriter nonce was 1 (no separate approve). Calldata decoded with my own hand-written ABI: selector 0x88e95e12 equals cast sig; terms, bond, nonce, v/r/s equal the intended values and the signature.

verified.claim: Signature cannot be replayed or used by someone else
verified.evidence: Resending the same signed tx reverted; sending it from a stranger account reverted. Step 2 refused a signature from the wrong signer, a tampered bond, nonce, validBefore, underwriter, market, an all-zero signature and a short signature.

verified.claim: Cover transactions: approve for exactly the deposit, then open
verified.evidence: Decoded with my own ABI: approve selector 0x095ea7b3 (cast sig), to=USDG, spender=the offer's cover (not the market), amount 100000000 exactly; open selector 0x20fb6636 (cast sig), to=offer cover, args limitBps 1000, rules {mask 3, stock 3000, trade 1000, daily 20000, slip 50, age 14400}, amount 100000000. Sent both: allowance after = 0, user spent 100000000, offer bond 500 -> 501 USDG, reserved 19800000, free 481200000. Reserved matches my reading of the contract: ceil(99e6*(3000-1000)/10000).

Decoded with my own ABI: selector 0xa284af6f (cast sig). The tool's decision hash equals keccak256 of the calldata decision bytes computed by viem and by cast keccak (0x320cfef9...37e3), and the canonical JSON with non-ASCII, quotes and nested arrays/objects matched my hand-written expectation. On chain (second run, correct event ABI): buy of 9 USDG emitted Traded and a sell of max emitted Traded; both event decisionHash values equal my independent keccak of the calldata bytes and sdk.verifyDecision returned ok true. Blocked events (TradeTooLarge for 10, 1000 and max buys; ZeroAmount for 0) also carried the same hash, state unchanged, no revert. A stranger sending the trade reverted.

verified.claim: Reference price equals the published vectors
verified.evidence: Live CLI quote for Careful's default rules: fairBps 13.09326229141971 (PRICING_VECTORS row 13.093262). Bold's rules (maxStockBps 8000) at 10% limit: 174.73609478944195 (vector 174.736095); at 20%: 47.29807625380319 (vector 47.298076).

verified.claim: Bad inputs are refused with readable messages
verified.evidence: Amounts -5, 1e2, 0x64, 1.0000001 (7 decimals), '', .5, '1,5', NaN, number 1e21 rejected; 0.999999 and number 1e-7 quoted as ok false (below the 1 USDG minimum). limit_bps 0, 499, 2001, 3000, 65536, -1 give problems; 10.5 rejected by schema. Unknown offer, market and asset, out-of-range rules (mask 0/255, stock 9000, slippage 501, price age 0 or huge, trade 70000, daily 100001), capacity overrun (10000 USDG), fee 501/70000, 65-byte name, zero agent, zero bond, non-JSON decision, 908-byte decision, min_out -1, 1.5 and 2^256, a non-account address, bad signatures and an unknown tool all produced errors (isError or MCP -32602), never a built transaction.

verified.claim: SDK and MCP hold no keys and send nothing
verified.evidence: grep of sdk/src, mcp/src and both bin folders for sendTransaction, privateKey, PRIVATE_KEY, walletClient, dotenv and .env found only the example file (which takes a caller's wallet) and process.env reads of RPC/records/raw-deployment variables. All six tools are annotated readOnlyHint.
After every run: no anvil process, nothing on port 8562, no deployments/raw-8562.json, no contracts/broadcast 8562 directory.

breakAttempts.attempt: Alter the bond, nonce, validBefore, underwriter or market in step 2 while reusing the real signature
breakAttempts.result: Refused each time (recovered signer differs, or unknown market).

breakAttempts.attempt: Alter terms.agent in step 2 (terms are not part of the signed EIP-3009 message)
breakAttempts.result: Accepted: the tool builds a transaction naming the swapped agent. Not a loss of funds, because only the underwriter's own transaction can use the signature and the decoded call args show the agent, but a hostile intermediary could swap terms. Worth one sentence in docs: decode before sending.

breakAttempts.attempt: Replay the signed create-offer tx, and send it from a stranger
Stranger sends an SDK-built trade for someone's account
Send decision as array, as non-JSON text, as 908 bytes, or with a 900-character reason
breakAttempts.result: Array rejected by schema, text and 908-byte object rejected, long reason shortened to fit (documented). The string 'null' is accepted as valid JSON and hashed as is.
Caught by validation as out of range, no encoder crash.

breakAttempts.attempt: usd_amount 0 or 'max' on a buy; min_out together with min_out_tolerance_bps
breakAttempts.result: Builds a transaction without complaint. On chain the contract records Blocked (ZeroAmount, TradeTooLarge) and nothing changes. min_out silently wins over the tolerance. Cosmetic.

breakAttempts.attempt: CLI with --offer abc, a missing flag, an invalid address or an unknown market
breakAttempts.result: Exits 1 but prints an uncaught-exception stack trace rather than a clean message (the unknown command path is clean, exit 2). Cosmetic.

breakAttempts.attempt: Run the shipped e2e as is
breakAttempts.result: Not done on purpose: it hardcodes port 8551 and I was limited to 8562. I ran a copy patched only for port, chain id and build folder; 10/10 and 8/8 pass.

summary: Everything the builder claimed reproduced. Unit (22), typecheck, e2e (10, on my port 8562 copy), MCP-over-stdio (8, same), live read-only (4) all pass. I decoded every SDK-built transaction with my own ABI and cast: selectors match, approve is exactly the deposit to the offer's cover, the decision hash equals keccak of the calldata bytes and the on-chain event hash, the typed-data domain equals the on-chain DOMAIN_SEPARATOR, and the reference prices match the published vectors. Bad inputs were refused with clear errors. Findings are minor: terms are not bound by the signature in step 2, the CLI shows raw stack traces on bad flags, and a zero or max buy is built (the contract then records Blocked). The shown tests use a mock USDG and Anvil keys, not testnet. Notes: I ran npm install as part of the literal quickstart (lockfile byte-identical); the harness copies and my scripts are in /Users/naitik/surety/verification/vc.
